Welcome to ACS International Schools
INSPIRING THE WORLD’S NEXT GLOBAL THINKERS AND DOERS
The ACS Mission
Established in 1967, central to our mission was our founders’ commitment to providing a high-quality, truly international education that nurtures global thinkers and doers and inspires better solutions to positively impact the communities we serve.
ACS International Schools became a registered UK charity in 2018. As a charity, ACS is committed to providing a range of means-tested bursary places and working both locally and internationally in collaboration with schools and communities to share expertise and resources, enriching the education of our partner communities and ourselves.
ACS at a glance
Our Schools
ACS Cobham
Situated in 128-acres of beautiful Surrey countryside, ACS Cobham offers world-class teaching and facilities for day and boarding students.
ACS Egham
A leading IB World School set in leafy Surrey, offering all four International Baccalaureate programmes for students aged 4-18.
ACS Hillingdon
A leading international school close to central London, known for its rigorous curriculum, thriving community, and exceptional facilities.
THE WORLD NEEDS NEW THINKING. GET READY!
Internationally-recognised curriculum
Our broad and challenging curriculum is designed to help our students excel, ensuring they are ready for the next stage of their academic career. Underpinned by the International Baccalaureate, Advanced Placement programmes and the High School Diploma, our curriculum emphasises life skills as much as academic ability, with a focus on community service and leadership that ensures we nurture confident, caring, and effective individuals.
Approach to Learning
A truly international community
With students from over 70 countries, we proudly cultivate a rich tapestry of experiences that empowers individuals to thrive. At ACS, we believe in fostering an environment that celebrates unique perspectives, cultures, and backgrounds. It’s ingrained in our curriculum, co-curricular activities, and everyday interactions, providing an educational journey that prepares students to become compassionate, global citizens.
A well-rounded, personalised approach
Our tailored approach and breadth of opportunities – both curricular and co-curricular – means students can follow their individual interests and ambitions for their future, so they leave ACS ready to stand out on the global stage.
Outstanding facilities
Our campuses boast state-of-the-art facilities that provide an inspiring environment for students to thrive academically, socially, and creatively. Our world-class facilities include modern classrooms equipped with the very latest technology, swimming pools and sports courts, well-stocked libraries, and creative art studios.
Explore our campuses and discover how our innovative facilities set the stage for a transformative educational journey.

Global Strategic Partners
Proudly partnering with the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra, ACS International Schools is set to elevate its arts education provision.
This collaboration grants ACS and partner school students exclusive access to world-class musical and production experiences, marking the initial phase of our envisioned Arts Pathway.
This strategic initiative aims to inspire creativity and foster the artistic growth of students, cultivating a supportive performing arts community within our schools. Our partnership with RPO represents a dynamic commitment to nurturing a holistic and enriched educational experience for our students, setting the stage for a vibrant and collaborative future in the performing arts.
RPO & ACS Events
ACS students and our partner schools will benefit from the expertise of the world renowned RPO. We are committed to our ongoing process of collaboration which serves to enrich the education of our wider partner communities and ourselves.
Partner with ACS
A true partnership offers something to everyone involved. Here at ACS, we are keen to explore relationships with other organisations and individuals.
ACS Egham RPO Summer Soiree

IB or A Levels: which will get you further?
Partnerships
ACS Partnerships
As a group of schools with an inspiring, engaged community and an international ethos, ACS is uniquely placed to build meaningful educational partnerships that advance education for school age children, supporting local and global communities wherever it can.
ACS Partnerships provide opportunity for students to access enhanced education not otherwise available to them and for teachers to develop teaching excellence.
On the global stage, ACS has two long term community school projects in Namibia and Nepal, offering our students and local school children a chance to connect and learn from each other. ACS was thrilled to win a silver award from the Global Good awards in recognition of its partnerships locally and internationally.
Our Impact
of student interaction
of teacher training
of outreach box usage
Community Collaboration
We collaborate with partner schools locally and globally. Partner schools use our facilities for many different occasions and uses, from hosting a sports day, attending our forest schools, to multi school learning and activity days hosted at our campuses.
This includes the SATROFest welcoming 21 Surrey senior schools for a day of STEM challenge, Destination Imagination UK, local primary school groups STEM festival, and countless school swimming galas.
ACS is committed to continuing to share resources, facilities, expertise, and ideas with partner schools and delighted to collaborate to enrich both local and ACS students’ learning experiences.
Partnerships events and activities
ACS creates memorable experiences for students to come together and learn through major events.
STEAM 2022 was a celebration of all things STEAM (science, technology, engineering, arts and mathematics) for 10,000 students, who attended a day at Thorpe Park theme park. Corporate exhibitors such as the Royal Air Force and the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra (RPO) attended for the students to engage with and learn from before enjoying the rides.
Other activities include: young carer days at our campuses; Elite football residential camps in partnerships with London premier league clubs; ‘A Night at the West End’ with 12 partner schools and 250 local school children performing alongside partners Performing Perfectly and the RPO.
So many of our pupils have gained transferable skills in terms of developing the confidence to take risks as well as the inspiration ACS has provided to prepare them for the world of work.
Teaching Excellence
ACS shares teaching excellence and a deep understanding of best practice to empower teachers within partner schools, often with limited or stretched resources, to advance their own skillset and students’ educational experience. ACS provides expertise and training in a number of ways:
Partnerships in action
A Night at the West End
Partnership Opportunities
Corporate partners
Partnership Schools
Use of ACS Facilities
Sponsorship
Corporate partners
We are keen to partner with external organisations to support opportunities identified to enhance the education of children at our member schools.
Access to industry expertise and resources is vital to the success of our partnership hub, and through close relationships with these organisations we can offer substantial experiential learning opportunities to students and staff.
Partnership Schools
There are three ACS Partnership Hubs based around our campuses in Cobham, Egham and Hillingdon. All schools within a 5-mile radius of these campuses are welcome to join.
No contracts or expectations, a community of staff across schools in the region will share best practice, informing each other and jointly supporting the students in their care.
Use of ACS Facilities
Wherever possible we will make our resources and facilities available to others to offer educational opportunities to school age children and school staff.
The ‘Use Our Resources/Facilities’ section of our Partnerships App will enable you to see which resources are available at our three campuses, browse our resources, risk assessments and procedures before getting in touch to see if we can accommodate your request.
Our facility priority will be to the students attending ACS Schools, but if a resource or facility is available, then we would gladly open it to local schools or businesses offering educational experiences or enhancement. We offer use of our performing arts centre; sports centre café; sports hall; dance studio; swimming pool; astroturf pitches; football pitches; science labs; meeting rooms and more.
Sponsorship
ACS we are keen to explore relationships with other organisations and individuals. A strong partnership helps young people recognise and achieve their potential, empowering them to take charge of their economic success. Get in touch today to discuss how we can work together.

AI at ACS
Artificial Intelligence at ACS: A Guide for Parents & Carers
Artificial intelligence, often shortened to AI, is part of our everyday lives. Students encounter it in search engines, games, social media, creative tools, and increasingly in learning.
At ACS International Schools, our approach to AI is thoughtful, cautious, and human centred. We see Artificial Intelligence as something students need to understand, question, and use responsibly, rather than something to fear or use uncritically.
This page is designed to support parents and carers, with a particular focus on how to talk with your child about AI use at school and beyond.
What do we mean by AI?
AI refers to computer systems that can generate text, images, audio, code, or recommendations by identifying patterns in large amounts of data.
Tools such as chatbots, image generators, recommendation systems, and automated feedback tools all use forms of AI.
AI systems do not think, understand, or make judgments in the way humans do. They generate outputs based on probability, patterns, and prior data. This is why human oversight, critical thinking, and ethical judgment remain essential.
Why does ACS engage with AI at all?
AI is already shaping the world our students are growing up in. Avoiding it altogether would leave young people unprepared. Our responsibility is to help students:
This approach aligns with ACS Opportunity Statements on Ethics and Academic Integrity (used by staff), which emphasise human dignity, fairness, transparency, and responsibility in the age of AI.
Protect their voice, creativity, and integrity.
Using AI at ACS
How is AI used at ACS?
Academic Integrity and Artificial Intelligence
Safeguarding, privacy, and wellbeing
How is AI used at ACS?
AI may be used in carefully guided ways to:
Alongside this, teachers help students think critically about AI by discussing its limitations, inaccuracies, and potential biases. These conversations are led by teachers and embedded in curriculum learning, rather than delegated to the technology itself.
AI is not a substitute for learning, thinking, or effort. Teachers set clear expectations about when and how AI tools may be used, and these expectations vary depending on age, subject, and task.
Our staff follow ACS guidelines for professional and classroom use of AI, which stress human judgment, transparency, and safeguarding.
Support brainstorming, planning, or idea generation.
Support accessibility, language development, or differentiation.
Academic Integrity and Artificial Intelligence
Learning is about developing skills, understanding, and personal voice. It is not necessarily about getting an answer correct – the learning lies in the ‘struggle’ of reaching (or perhaps never reaching!) the answers. Using AI to bypass that process undermines learning.
We also recognise that boundaries are evolving. Rather than relying on detection software alone, teachers are moving towards a focus on assessment design, in class processes, and conversations with students about their learning choices.
Safeguarding, privacy, and wellbeing
ACS places student safety and wellbeing at the centre of all technology decisions.
AI raises important questions about identity, agency, and what it means to be human. These are explored thoughtfully in a range of curriculum contexts, rather than left unexamined.
We prioritise age appropriate use
We discuss misinformation, deepfakes, and manipulation explicitly
Talking to your child about AI: practical tips
One of the most important things parents and carers can do is keep the conversation open. You do not need to be a technical expert. Curiosity and values matter more than technical detail. Here are some prompts and approaches that can help.
Ask your child how they are using AI
Focus on learning, not just rules
Reinforce human values
Talk about risks and responsibilities
These conversations mirror the guidance shared at ACS and align with current advice for parents and carers about emerging technologies.
Your ideas, experiences, and voice matter
Struggle can be productive and meaningful
AI can be biased or confidently wrong
A human-centred approach
Our approach to AI is grounded in the belief that technology should serve human flourishing.
AI is treated as a tool, not an authority.
Keeping humans in the loop
Valuing creativity, judgment, empathy, and integrity
Questioning power, bias, and commercial influence
Further reading and resources
If you have questions or concerns about AI use at ACS, we encourage you to contact your child’s school. Open dialogue between home and school is one of the most important safeguards we have.

Leadership Team
Robert Harrison
Robert Harrison
Robert Harrison is an accomplished education executive with a lifelong commitment to learning and teaching. He holds a PhD in Religion and Sociology from Duke University and has built a career defined by high-impact leadership across public, private, and charitable sectors around the world.
After years as a special educator and teacher leader in Washington, D.C., Robert joined the International Baccalaureate (IB) in 2010. There, he served as the first manager for global education and later as Head of Middle Years Programme (MYP) Development in The Hague. During his tenure, he led the worldwide implementation of “MYP: Next Chapter” and spearheaded the development of the innovative MYP eAssessment.
After his initial appointment in 2018 as ACS’s first Education Strategy Director, from 2022 to 2026 Robert was Director of Education and Integrated Technology. Bridging the gap between teaching and commercial operations, he helped deliver robust business systems and integrated processes that modernized the group’s infrastructure. His leadership was instrumental in establishing a comprehensive education quality framework, resulting in measurable excellence in both academic outcomes and school climate.
A frequent author, speaker, and former co-editor-in-chief of the IB Journal of Teaching Research, Robert continues to drive strategy at the intersection of curriculum design and technological transformation.
Graeme Lawrie MBE
Director of Operations
Graeme Lawrie MBE
Director of Operations
Graeme is Chief Operating Officer at ACS International Schools, with strategic responsibility for IT, HR, Marketing, Partnerships and operational delivery across the organisation. A qualified teacher with over two decades of experience in education, he brings a distinctive perspective as a senior leader who has progressed through the profession from classroom teacher to executive leadership.
Graeme began his career at Oakham School as a teacher and house parent, before joining Sevenoaks School in 2006 as Head of Department. In 2009 he became Head of Faculty for Science, where he led the development of one of the world’s largest free science events in the UK at the time. He went on to hold a number of senior leadership roles including Director of Innovation and Excellence, and Director of Outreach and Innovation, building a reputation for delivering large scale, high impact educational initiatives.
Throughout his career, Graeme has combined educational leadership with operational and strategic delivery, leading complex programmes, managing multi-disciplinary teams, and building partnerships across sectors. His work has focused on widening access to opportunity, developing innovative approaches to education, and ensuring that organisations operate effectively in support of their core mission.
In addition to his school-based leadership, Graeme has worked with OCR, AQA and the International Baccalaureate, contributing to curriculum and assessment development. He also completed a yearlong secondment at Buckingham Palace as a Special Advisor to the Royal Family in 2015.
Graeme was awarded an MBE in the Queen’s Birthday Honours 2020 for services to education. He has received multiple national awards, including the Lloyds TSB Teacher of the Year and Pearson Teacher of the Year, and was named by TES as one of the top five science teachers in the UK.
He remains passionate about social mobility and the role education plays in transforming lives, having worked with hundreds of schools, charities and international communities to create meaningful opportunities for young people.
Outside of work, Graeme enjoys climbing, motorsport and engineering projects, and spending time with his family.
Martin Hall
Head of School, ACS Hillingdon
Martin Hall
Head of School, ACS Hillingdon
Martin Hall grew up in Scotland and gained his first degree in Political Economy and Philosophy from the University of Glasgow.
He taught Economics, Business Studies, and History at highly regarded state schools in England, and then at a Tanzanian school for two years with the VSO. Martin served as Secondary Principal at the Inter-Community School of Zurich, and most recently, as Director of the International School of Tanganyika in Tanzania. He is an experienced member and co-Chair of accreditation teams and was a Board member of the Association of International Schools in Africa. Martin has a Masters in Educational Leadership from the Open University, and the National Professional Qualification for Headship.
As a school leader, Martin has continued teaching such classes as Economics and Theory of Knowledge, valuing the continued opportunity to develop his professional practice and interact directly with students. Martin is committed to the culture of excellence in schools, setting high aspirations for students and encouraging critical thinking throughout the school community. He is passionate about supporting student achievement and well-being through effective pastoral systems and nurturing student engagement.
Mark Wilson
Head of School, ACS Egham
Mark Wilson
Head of School, ACS Egham
Mark Wilson has been teaching and leading schools for over 27 years. He started his career in the UK before moving into International Education by joining Nord Anglia Education in 2009 at The British International School Shanghai as a Headteacher. Mark then moved to the US and was Head of School at The British International School of Houston.
Mark trained as a Drama teacher and has taught a range of subjects over the years at GCSE, A Level, BTEC and IBDP. He still teaches Theory of Knowledge on the IB Programme.
Inspiring others to learn and grow is one of Marks passions and throughout his career he has been privileged to be involved in teacher training, working with a variety of universities and providers including, Middlesex, Nottingham and Sunderland Universities as well as the Royal Academy of Dance. Mark was fortunate to have worked for the UK Department of Education Innovations Unit on Leadership projects. Within Nord Anglia Education he taught or coached on the NAE Middle Leaders and the NEA Senior Leaders courses and wrote and facilitated the Americas Aspiring Leaders programme.
Robert Crowther
Head of School, ACS Cobham
Robert Crowther
Head of School, ACS Cobham
Robert’s journey to ACS has had many stops along the way. British by birth, raised in Australia, educated in Australia and the UK and living and working internationally since 1991.
Robert’s international school career has taken him to Rome, Frankfurt, Berlin, Ho Chi Minh City and Jakarta. In that time, he has taught in Lower Schools as well as Middle School English and Mathematics and Learning Support. He has been a divisional Principal, Assistant Principal, Head of School, Curriculum Coordinator, teacher trainer and member of authorisation teams for the International Baccalaureate Organisation.

Our History
Back in 1967 our founders opened their first school with one division and 35 students. Today ACS is a leader in the field of international education, enrolling 2,400 students, aged 2-18, at 3 schools in Greater London.
Mr. Speed was born into a Scottish-American family living in Florida USA, where he attended school and received his MA from Florida State University. After teaching in Florida, the Dominican Republic, France and Italy, Mr Speed moved to London in 1965.
Mr. Poularas was born in 1943 into a Greek-Armenian family living in Port Said, Egypt. He came to London in 1962 and quickly progressed in the maritime industry. Mr. Poularas passed away in 2008, just before ACS's 40th anniversary, while Mr. Speed also left us in 2019, marking ACS's 52nd year.
The ACS character Mr Speed and Mr Poularas created all those years ago remains fresh and constant – a genuinely caring, engaged community with a strong sense of its role and responsibilities to the local and global families we serve. A place where innovative teaching drives a dynamic learning environment.

Relocation Professionals
At ACS International Schools, we understand that relocating — whether internationally or within the UK — is an exciting journey for any family, but we also know it can feel daunting.
That’s why we provide a warm, supportive welcome to help new families settle into both our school community and their new surroundings.
Our goal is to ensure every member of the ACS community feels included and engaged from day one. We’re committed to making the transition as smooth and positive as possible, offering guidance and encouragement every step of the way.
Find out how we service the needs of all families and global relocation industry, as well as information about past relocation events and opportunities to attend future events.
We are pleased to announce that we have recently won an award in the Schools & Education Consultant category at the ARP 35th Anniversary Awards.
Relocation at ACS
ACS is an active member of the relocation community, with a strong network of contacts dedicated to helping new families adapt to their new surroundings.
We’re proud members of the Association of Relocation Professionals (ARP), the European Relocation Association (EuRA), and Admissions, Marketing and Communications in Independent Schools (AMCIS). We’re also featured in FOCUS magazine.
Both FOCUS and Relocate magazines offer excellent resources for expatriates moving to the UK, providing valuable insights and practical advice to support a smooth transition.
I would like to sincerely thank you for the warm and welcoming event at ACS Egham. The atmosphere was incredibly positive, and your staff were exceptionally kind and helpful. It was clear from the very first moment how friendly and close-knit the ACS Egham community truly is.
Language
Transition
Community
Language
ACS International Schools provide a supportive and enriching environment that values diversity and inclusion.
Although the primary language spoken at ACS is English, our three schools (Cobham, Egham and Hillingdon) are known for embracing EAL (English as Additional Language) students, offering specialist support for all age groups.
ACS has over 2400 students from 70 countries, and teaches a wide-breadth of different languages.
Transition
All ACS families have access to The Wellbeing Hub — a trusted, expert-designed resource that supports the social, emotional, and educational needs of young people.
As part of our commitment to helping new families settle in, ACS offers a range of transition activities tailored to the time of year they join. The post-admittance journey begins with access to our Admissions Hub, and new families are added to a list shared with the Parent Support Organisation (PSO), ensuring they’re warmly welcomed by the parent community. For students moving from Lower to Upper School, we also organise ‘bump-up’ transition sessions led by faculty, helping them prepare for the next stage of their education.
Throughout the year, ACS hosts a variety of events to help new families connect and feel at home. During the summer, our informal ice-cream social brings families onto campus to start building relationships in a relaxed, friendly setting. Just before the start of the school year, we hold a new student orientation, featuring introductions to key staff members and ‘market stalls’ providing information on buses, clubs, music, and more.
Once the school year begins, the PSO continues to foster community spirit with events like the welcome BBQ in September and the International Fair in the spring. Together with the ACS Admissions team, these events ensure every new family feels supported and included from day one.
Community
Each ACS campus has its own Parent Support Organisation (PSO), made up of dedicated volunteer parents who work to strengthen connections between the school, students, and families through a range of social, charitable, and informational events. A key focus of the PSO is welcoming new families and helping them settle into both the school and the local area — a role they fulfil year-round through events and regular communications.
Once you’ve joined ACS, the PSO Welcome Committee will reach out ahead of your arrival, providing useful information and helping to make your transition as smooth as possible. At ACS Hillingdon, the PSO also assigns a ‘Buddy’ family, either from the same grade or neighbourhood, offering an extra layer of support.
ACS is also an active member of local community groups that help families settle into their new surroundings. We’re proud to be Gold sponsors of American Wives of Surrey (AWS) and All Women in Berkshire and Surrey (AWBS) — both of which offer a fantastic community for women new to the area, with regular meet-ups and trips to London and beyond.
Get in touch!
If you would like to arrange a time to meet at one of the ACS campuses we would be delighted to give you a personal tour and have you meet our Head of School and Admissions teams. Alternatively we can arrange an in-person meeting at your offices, at a mutually convenient location, or via Zoom.

pageCache.pageTitle: Forging the way in Science and Technology - ACS International Schools
pageCache.text:
IB or A Levels: which will get you further?
At ACS, we believe education should never stand still. The world our students will inherit is changing at an unprecedented pace, shaped by technologies that blur the boundaries between disciplines, industries and cultures. For today’s learners, technology is not a separate entity; it is seamlessly integrated into their lives. As a leading international school group, we believe our responsibility is to ensure students don’t just keep up with change, but help shape it – embedding technology as an integral part of learning across subjects and real-world contexts
This is why at ACS we talk less about ‘STEM’ or ‘STEAM’ and more about the future-ready skills our students develop every day. Adaptability, risk-taking, creativity, empathy, collaboration and problem-solving are at the heart of our learning ethos. These qualities transcend individual subjects and prepare young people not just to succeed in the workplace, but to make a meaningful impact on society.
Fostering future-ready skills
We believe that the right skills and the right environments go hand in hand. Students need opportunities to practise collaboration, creativity and problem-solving, but they also need spaces that inspire and support this kind of learning.
Our innovative science and tech labs are designed to be flexible and multi-purpose, encouraging teamwork and cross-disciplinary inquiry. They are equipped with the latest tools, from robotics and digital media suites to 3D printers and laser cutters, but these spaces only reach their potential when combined with project-based, hands-on learning. Teachers play a vital role in unlocking that potential, ensuring every lab or creative hub is used to spark curiosity and innovation.
This approach ensures that ACS students are not confined by traditional rows of desks. Instead, they learn in dynamic environments that mirror the world they will one day work in, developing transferable skills in spaces designed for creativity and discovery.
Authentic Intelligence
In an age dominated by artificial intelligence, ACS champions something even more important: authentic intelligence. This is our belief that the future will not be defined by machines alone, but by the uniquely human qualities that allow us to work alongside technology.
Authentic intelligence combines empathy, ethics, creativity and resilience with digital fluency. Our students are not only learning how to use technology but also how to question it, shape it and engage with it responsibly. In all our schools, technology integration is purposeful and thoughtful. Students learn through real-world applications, whether building earthquake-resistant Lego models in Lower School, producing digital art, or exploring the globe through Google Earth. By going deeper with fewer platforms, they gain mastery and confidence rather than surface-level familiarity.
We see technology not as an end in itself, but as a tool to enhance learning, spark innovation and support human development.
Innovation in Action
Innovation at ACS is not defined by the tools alone, but by how students use them to explore, experiment and create. Robotics, 3D printing, digital media and design technology provide powerful platforms, yet what sets us apart is our focus on what comes next. We encourage students to look beyond what is already possible, to ask bold questions and to pioneer new solutions.
That is why we are exploring emerging areas such as electronics, Arduino programming, immersive media and advanced coding. These fields not only offer exciting opportunities for students but also position ACS to stay ahead of the curve. By continually asking “what is next?” we ensure that our facilities and curriculum remain relevant, dynamic and inspiring.
Innovation at ACS extends beyond traditional labs. Our students are encouraged to pursue challenging opportunities to innovate beyond the curriculum, through participation in a wide range of clubs and activities. ACS teams continue to enter prestigious local and national competitions and tournaments, our students are successful competitors and prize winners in the First Lego League robotics challenge, the Destination Imagination innovation challenge, the European Space Agency Satellite Simulation Competition, F1 in Schools, and the RaspberryPi Mission Zero Challenge (our students had their code run on the International Space Station!).
Our Esports programme is another powerful example of innovation beyond the traditional classroom. Far more than gaming, Esports builds teamwork, leadership, data analysis and decision-making under pressure. With Esports now a global industry worth billions, ACS is preparing students for opportunities in one of the fastest-growing sectors of the 21st century. Just as importantly, Esports reflects the way students already engage with technology, making it a natural and compelling platform for developing transferable skills.
At ACS, our edge lies in the skills and human qualities we cultivate. We grow adaptable, creative, ethical and resilient learners who see themselves as capable of shaping the future. Our classrooms are alive with collaboration, our labs spark innovation and our projects build confidence and purpose.
By combining authentic intelligence with adaptable spaces and transferable capabilities, ACS ensures that its students are not just prepared for the future, they are already shaping it.
